svg.title: Cluster throughput from 4 to 96 vCPU, no message lost at any point
svg.desc: Columns of the cluster's msg/s at its number of vCPU, on a linear axis, one panel per workload; under each column its shape as nodes × vCPU each and what its hardware costs a month per 1M msg/s, every host priced at AWS m6a.8xlarge's on-demand rate ($0.0432 a vCPU-hour, 730 hours a month), no licence. The green part is the highest step carried at p99 ≤ 1 s; a yellow cap reaches the maximum lossless step when it ran at p99 ≤ 5 s, a red cap when it ran above; a dashed outline is a vendor's published figure; ≥ marks a floor, whose cost is then at most the one printed. Durable QoS 1, 1 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 23.2k msg/s per vCPU, 92,900 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; ack p99 744 ms; 1 copy, fsync only), $1,358 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; Durable QoS 1, 3 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 9.8k msg/s per vCPU, 117,800 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; ack p99 1.35 s), $3,212 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; 114,200 msg/s at p99 ≤ 1 s (ack p99 708 ms); Durable QoS 1, 1 × 32 vCPU (AWS m6i.8xlarge): 2.8k msg/s per vCPU, 88,700 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; ack p99 300 ms; 1 copy, fsync only), $11,377 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; Durable QoS 1, 10 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 7.3k msg/s per vCPU, 292,200 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; ack p99 1.37 s), $4,317 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; 228,000 msg/s at p99 ≤ 1 s (ack p99 59 ms); Durable QoS 1, 6 × 16 vCPU (AWS m6i.4xlarge): 4.1k msg/s per vCPU, 390,300 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; ack p99 112 ms; the next step, 400,800, lost 4,145 (append-backlog-full) in one round of 3), $7,757 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; HiveMQ 4.18 (published), 3 × 32 vCPU (AWS m6a.8xlarge): 270,000 msg/s, 2.8k per vCPU, published, not reproduced; QoS 1, clean sessions, 1 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 28.5k msg/s per vCPU, 114,000 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; ack p99 315 ms), $1,107 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; QoS 1, clean sessions, 3 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 22.6k msg/s per vCPU, 270,800 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; ack p99 3.31 s), $1,397 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; 152,000 msg/s at p99 ≤ 1 s (ack p99 67 ms); QoS 1, clean sessions, 10 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 21.9k msg/s per vCPU, 875,900 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; ack p99 4.54 s), $1,440 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; 303,800 msg/s at p99 ≤ 1 s (ack p99 85 ms); QoS 0, 1 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 30.8k msg/s per vCPU, 123,100 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; end-to-end p99 136 ms), $1,025 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; QoS 0, 3 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 28.4k msg/s per vCPU, 340,300 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; end-to-end p99 2.52 s), $1,112 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; 253,200 msg/s at p99 ≤ 1 s (end-to-end p99 547 ms); QoS 0, 10 × 4 vCPU (Hetzner CCX23): 24.3k msg/s per vCPU, 973,200 msg/s in total with no message lost (maximum lossless; end-to-end p99 4.49 s), $1,296 of hardware a month per 1M msg/s; 506,300 msg/s at p99 ≤ 1 s (end-to-end p99 395 ms).
svg.text: Cluster throughput from 4 to 96 vCPU, no message lost at any point
cluster msg/s from the brokers' own counters · 3 rounds a step · main edfdb49, 9520b33 and 19f36004, 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-31
p99 is the ack latency for QoS 1 and the end-to-end latency for QoS 0, the mean of the rounds
ack after fsync + a quorum copy · 1 node keeps one copy
vCPU in the cluster · nodes × vCPU each · $ a month per 1M msg/s

vCPU in the cluster · nodes × vCPU each · $ a month per 1M msg/s
brokers: Hetzner CCX23 (4 vCPU), AWS m6i.4xlarge (16 vCPU) and AWS m6i.8xlarge (32 vCPU) · load generators calibrated before the ladder · $share, 200 B · 60 s windows
$ a month per 1M msg/s: hardware only, priced at AWS m6a.8xlarge's on-demand rate, $0.0432 a vCPU-hour × 730 h (Hetzner's is about the same) · no licence
